title: Phase 1: the reconciler and the local subprocess executor
description: SPEC §12 Phase 1 (docs/projects/2026-09-01-ticfac-architecture/SPEC.md (in pengelbrecht/ticks)). Mirrors epic 4ik in the ticks tracker, which holds the roadmap; this epic holds the code ticks because ticks is one tracker per repository. Build the deterministic lifecycle in code — claims, waves, gates, merge, boundary checks, cleanup ordering — as a restartable reconciler for one epic at concurrency one, and the local subprocess executor behind the four-operation protocol (start/inspect/cancel/collect) with claude, codex and pi as runner values. ticfac talks to ticks ONLY through tk --json (contract 1, contracts/tk-json-manifest.json) and the pinned contract bundle 3.0.0; every contract gets a ticfac Go reader. Do not build an event bus, plugin system, or same-repo multi-epic execution to make the gate pass. Legacy defects that must be solved by design (from ticks epic 72y, recorded on 4ik): executor-owned RESULT path; identity (repo key, run, tick, attempt); boundary on tracker records only with config exempt; diff against the recorded attempt base; timer push; in-flight state settled by whoever finds it next; finished-worker detection from durable evidence with no lost-event race; zero orphaned worktrees after cleanup.

Route to a repair wave or defer? → One more repair wave (9): 604 = sandbox bare-relative-path bypass + honest claims (subprocess); 0c1 = refusal teardown incl. role-job, cancel.json on settled attempts, spent() vs local branch, gate-failure recovery (reconcile). This supersedes the earlier 7mj-scope decision on role-job worktrees. — A read-only grade that a bare path defeats, and a resumable run that mislabels or orphans work, are the epic's own A6/A9/A10 invariants; fixing now is cheaper than after Phase 2 builds on them.
2026-09-09 16:06 - decision: 0c1 reported a false-close path (commit + STATUS: BLOCKED is merged and closed). Fix now or defer? → Fix now as wave 10 tick lo3, blocking the final review — A false close violates the epic's own no-false-success acceptance; it is a small seam change with a clear test.
2026-09-09 16:47 - decision: 604 acceptance lists 'a worker cannot push via a longer url.<prefix>.pushInsteadOf' and 'cannot push via a -c remote.<x>.url override' — the tests assert the opposite (the push lands). Amend the acceptance or treat as unmet? → Amend both lines to a stated residual: env-pinned push urls close the ACCIDENTAL push; a runner that brings its own credential or overrides its launch config is not stopped by the issuer, and the boundary diff at collect is the backstop. — git's longest-prefix rule for url.<prefix>.pushInsteadOf and the precedence of -c over env config are properties of git itself; no issuer-side pin can beat them. Closing them would need a credential-less transport or a pre-push hook the runner also controls. The tests now assert the true behaviour so a future regression is visible, the residual is stated identically in grade.go, doc.go, profiles and review-epic.md, and the upstream contract prose is filed as ticks of9. Same precedent as the AC5 amendment.
2026-09-09 16:55 - decision: The gcx final review found two blockers in the wave 9/10 repair surface: a merge refusal destroys the report the next collect reads, and a passing gate check is reused at a different commit. Route into this epic or to the backlog? → Into this epic as wave 11 tick o3n (P1, blocks gcx), together with three should-fix items on the same surface; the two remaining should-fix items are routed separately. — Both blockers were introduced or exposed by the wave 9/10 repairs themselves, so they are regressions in this epic's own diff rather than pre-existing debt. Each has a concrete failure scenario verified against the merged tree: a merge conflict becomes a permanent collect_failed missing-result, and a check that passed at commit A closes a tick at commit B. Closing gcx over either would ship the epic with a known way to lose a worker's verdict.
2026-09-09 17:36 - decision: o3n's gate-rekey fix (a pass is evidence only about the commit it ran on) makes an existing test fail: a restart now re-runs a gate it already paid for. The cause is the item o3n was told to leave out — GateSHA is the LIVE integration head, and the run-state store's own .ticfac records land on that same branch, so the head always differs. Fold that item in, or revert the blocker fix? → Fold it in: key the gate's evidence by the SOURCE tree under test (the gated commit's top-level tree with the .ticfac entry dropped) rather than by the raw commit. — The two are one problem, not two. Keying by raw commit is either too loose (reuse a pass across a real tree change, the blocker) or too tight (re-pay the gate because the run wrote its own records to the branch it gates). Neither can be fixed alone: reverting leaves a tick closable on evidence from a different tree, and landing the rekey alone makes every resume re-run the whole gate. A source fingerprint that ignores the run's own bookkeeping is the one key that is correct in both directions. Verified empirically: on a restart the epic head moved from 9791a24 to e84fbe2 with the only difference being .ticfac/runs/r-fixture/attempts/1.json.
2026-09-10 08:13 - decision: The gcx final review's remaining findings — settle's containment question surviving a revert (z8b), four operational failures raised as merge refusals (0bz), and Cancel serving two callers where only one wants a cancellation record (bgr) — block gcx, or ship Phase 1 and route them? → Route all three as follow-up ticks and close gcx. None is a correctness hole in what Phase 1 claims; each needs a design decision rather than a patch. — z8b and bgr are edge cases that need an operator either way and whose repair changes a contract (a settle escape hatch, or splitting Cancel into stop-versus-revoke); patching either blind at final review would be the kind of unreviewed change this round just caught twice. 0bz is pre-existing, predates the epic, and its repair touches the refusal vocabulary every caller switches on. All three are recorded with their failure scenarios and the decision each needs, and settle's refusal now names the revert case in prose so an operator meeting it is not left with a false premise. The epic's acceptance is met, the gate is green on b0d20c5, and holding Phase 1 open for three design questions would be scope the roadmap owns, not the epic.
acceptance_criteria: Gate: one real epic in the ticks repository completes through ticfac run-epic locally with a claude or codex runner, killed and restarted after dispatch, after collection and before closure, with no duplicate work and no false success; the Appendix A conformance suite (contracts/lifecycle-invariants.json, bundle 3.0.0) is green against the real reconciler and executor; the run leaves a .ticfac/runs/<id>/ record and a ticfac/run-<id> tag; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... (make test-short) green; CI verifies the pinned bundle.
